text: The legacy AC3 and AC7 of RWB-E1-013 are read as superseded by DP-17: no INT-19 extract, no data-lake load area, no freshness-stamped extract file, no trailer count and no Power BI data set is built, and the publish and the hold of the baseline move to the P9 publication with this service supplying the gate.
why: DP-17 removes the data lake, INT-19 and INT-20 (Arch v5 slides 8, 37 and 41), and no source restates AC3 or AC7 on a target path.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 37, 41 and 44; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-17; Interface Specifications v3 removal note.
applied_in: §2 Business rationale; §8 BR5 with BR9; §16 note on TC-E1-013-03 and TC-E1-013-07; §18 Traceability; §19 Out of scope
impact: The story builds no lake path and asserts none; a reviewer looking for the legacy lake step finds the gap row and the DP-17 reading instead.

text: The lake steps of FSD P1 A2.12 and A2.13, the INT-19 row of TSD P1 T5.1 and the table lake_copy_watermark are recorded as outdated and removed, and only the reconciliation result and the publish status of the case list are built.
why: The two P1 specifications predate the DP-17 removal and the ownership map gives lake_copy_watermark no target, so a literal reading would build a destination that does not exist.
read: FSD P1 A2.12.2 and A2.13.2; TSD P1 v3 T5.1 and T3.6; ownership map ruling on lake_copy_watermark.
applied_in: §12.6 Schedules; §12.7 Tables owned; §17 Guardrails (DP-17); §19 Out of scope
impact: Documentation only: no P1 table, file or interface of the lake survives into this service, and the data architect corrects the two specifications in the next versions.

text: RWB-E1-013 is split as follows and this story owns only the fourth part: RWB-P9-E1013-APP owns AC1, AC4, AC5, AC7 and AC8 and the whole measures pipeline; RWB-P3-E1013-APP owns the case facts; RWB-ITG-E1013-ITG owns the cross-service proof of AC2 and AC6; RWB-P1-E1013-APP owns the readiness, the gate, the payments, the two events, the two activities and JOB-04. AC3 and AC7 are removed by DP-17 rather than reassigned.
why: No source document assigns each legacy acceptance criterion to a new story, and the integration slice already uses this assignment, so the story follows it to keep the four slices consistent.
read: Architecture v5 slide 15 and slide 41; the integration story RWB-ITG-E1013-ITG sections 2, 18 and 19; ownership map on measure_definition, measure_snapshot, case_list_row and reconciliation_result.
applied_in: §2 Business rationale; §7 note below the feature; §16 note on the nine test cases; §18 Traceability story table; §19 Out of scope
confirm: Business analyst, P1, P3 and P9
impact: No legacy criterion is owned twice or left unowned except AC3 and AC7, which are recorded as removed; the four stories cite each other.

text: The 05:30 late check is a Temporal Schedule of the workflow platform in rwb-source-data, and the registration of that Schedule, of the two workers, of the task queue and of the topic belongs to the platform workflow and operations stories of the epic; this secondary slice records the dependency as a note and builds against the registered platform, so its build dependency row stays None.
why: DP-10 gives the pattern with H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, but the story that registers this service's Schedule and workers is named by no source and the Work Package fixes the build dependency of this slice as None.
read: Architecture v5 slides 31, 32 and 44; TSD P1 v3 T3.7; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-10 and §R5.7.
applied_in: §3 Preconditions (last point); §12.6 Schedules; §13 Pattern application; §15 Screens and states (DP-19)
confirm: DevOps team and platform workflow owner
impact: The story cannot be demonstrated in SIT until the Schedule and the worker are registered; the gap is carried as an operations dependency of the plan, not as a blocker of the build.

text: This story supplies the facts and the gate of the baseline and never a measure: it computes no measure value, holds no definition version, sets no baseline or frozen flag and reads neither measure_definition nor measure_snapshot, which stay in rwb_reporting with P9.
why: The ownership map gives both measure tables to P9 and the Architecture v5 catalogue gives rwb-reporting the measures and snapshots, so a measure value in this service would be a second count of one number.
read: Ownership map on measure_definition and measure_snapshot; Arch v5 slide 15 (P1 OUT and P9 OUT); TSD P1 v3 T3.6.
applied_in: §2 Business rationale; §7 note below the feature; §8 BR13; §11 Data (last two rows and the paragraph); §17 Guardrails
impact: The legacy figures of AC2 and AC6 are asserted by RWB-P9-E1013-APP and RWB-ITG-E1013-ITG; this story's tests assert only its own operations, events, activities and reconciliation rows.

text: The four operations of this story use the paths already called by the integration slice - POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/business-days/{date}/ready, GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/business-days/{date}/status, GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness and GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/payments?accountId={accountId} - with 202 on the first and on a repeat call and the three status values RUNNING, DONE and LATE; the response field names follow the field IDs of the P1 logical data model until the contract story fixes them.
why: The architecture fixes the two readiness paths, the 202, the idempotency and the three status values, and the API Specification and TSD P1 appendix name neither the readiness, the status nor the payments path, so the paths the integration suite calls are the only fixed ones.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 and slide 32 interface contract line; TSD P1 v3 appendix T-A; integration story RWB-ITG-E1013-ITG section 12.2.
applied_in: §4 Flow; §9 State transitions; §12.1 REST operations provided; §12.8 Contract fakes
confirm: Solution architect and TechX contract owner
impact: If the P1 OpenAPI document fixes other paths or field names, this story renames its controller paths and its response fields and no rule, value or test datum changes.

text: The freshness stamp of a product keeps LOADED or STALE from LOV-FRESHNESS and the daily gate of a business date answers COMPLETE or HOLD; the two vocabularies describe one condition at two levels and neither replaces the other.
why: Both are given by a source, and collapsing them would change either the stamp the decision log records or the gate answer the publication reads.
read: TSD P1 v3 T3.7 and T3.8 (LOV-FRESHNESS); integration story RWB-ITG-E1013-ITG section 9.
applied_in: §9 State transitions; §12.1 REST operations provided; §13 Components (FreshnessGate)
impact: A client reads the gate for the date and the status per product; no client reads one value where the other is expected, and the next P1 TSD version documents both lists.

text: MSG-P1-001 is raised with the FSD P1 and TSD P1 wording, "{product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived.", in the gate answer, the run record and the banner of this service, while the legacy story and the integration copy keep "Today's load has not arrived".
why: Under R-PREC the technical and functional specifications outrank the story masters, and the FSD open point OQ-P1-07 records that the message now names the ACE batch rather than a load.
read: FSD P1 VR-P1-001-1 and OQ-P1-07; TSD P1 v3 T3.7; RWB-E1-013 section 14.
applied_in: §7 Background and AC2; §8 BR12; §14 Validation and messages
impact: The ID and both placeholders are identical, so no test key changes; the message standard and the legacy copy need the same sentence before the wording is asserted end to end.
